New machine. Its objects are: gakalin, sopufa, pikanir, goramel, tekutas, mofiko.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by placing half of the objects on the machine to see how it responds.

TEST: gakalin, sopufa, pikanir
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The set {gakalin, sopufa, pikanir} lit up, but I don't yet know the rule. It might light for any nexiom, or only when both are present. Testing single objects will help with both questions.

TEST: gakalin
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Gakalin alone did not light the machine. If any single nexiom lights it, then gakalin is not a nexiom and sopufa or pikanir is. If both nexioms are needed, the pair is somewhere in {gakalin, sopufa, pikanir}. Testing sopufa alone separates these two cases: if it lights up, single nexioms are enough and sopufa is one of them.

TEST: sopufa
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Gakalin and sopufa each failed to light the machine alone, so there are two main possibilities:
- **One nexiom is enough to light it:** then pikanir must be a nexiom (it is the only object left from the first lit group), and the other nexiom is goramel, tekutas or mofiko.
- **Both nexioms are needed:** then the pair is inside {gakalin, sopufa, pikanir}.

Testing pikanir alone tells these apart:
- **If it lights up,** pikanir is a nexiom. I then have 2 tests to find which of the remaining three objects is the other.
- **If it doesn't,** the machine needs both nexioms. I then have 2 tests to pick the right pair from the three candidate pairs.

TEST: pikanir
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Pikanir lit the machine on its own. Gakalin and sopufa alone did not, so a lone non-nexiom does not light it. That makes pikanir a nexiom, and a single nexiom is enough to light the machine. The other nexiom must be goramel, tekutas or mofiko. I'll test goramel alone: if it lights, it's the second nexiom; if not, one more test separates tekutas from mofiko.

TEST: goramel
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Pikanir is a nexiom, and a single nexiom is enough to light the machine. Goramel did not light alone, so it is not a nexiom. That leaves tekutas or mofiko as the second one. Testing tekutas alone settles it: if it lights, tekutas is the nexiom; if not, mofiko is.

TEST: tekutas
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Tekutas lit the machine on its own, so it is the second nexiom. All five results fit a single rule: the machine lights whenever at least one nexiom is on it. Gakalin, sopufa and goramel never lit it alone. The first test lit up because pikanir was in the group. This assumes the rule is that simple, but nothing in the results contradicts it.

ANSWER: nexioms = pikanir, tekutas
One last question. If only pikanir were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

Yes. I tested exactly this in my fourth test, with pikanir alone on the machine, and it lit up. This was observed directly, not inferred.

PROBE: yes

New machine. Its objects are: kividok, notuner, rikolu, menesol, gugaben, munavin.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll begin by testing half of the objects to see whether the machine lights up when some of them are present.

TEST: kividok, notuner, rikolu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine lit up with kividok, notuner and rikolu. I don't know the rule yet: it might light for one nexiom or need both. Testing a single object will help narrow both questions.

TEST: kividok
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Kividok alone did not light the machine. So under either an "any one nexiom" rule or a "both nexioms" rule, at least one of notuner or rikolu is a nexiom. Testing notuner alone will tell me whether a single nexiom is enough to light it.

TEST: notuner
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Notuner alone lit the machine, so one nexiom is enough to light it. That makes notuner a nexiom. Kividok alone did not light, so kividok is not a nexiom. The second nexiom is among rikolu, menesol, gugaben and munavin. I'll test each one alone, since that works whether the rule is "at least one" or "exactly one" nexiom.

TEST: rikolu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Notuner is one nexiom. Kividok and rikolu did not light up alone, so neither is a nexiom. The second nexiom must be menesol, gugaben or munavin. I'll test menesol alone. If it doesn't light, I'll test gugaben, and if that doesn't light either, munavin must be the second one.

TEST: menesol
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Here is what the tests show so far:
- **Notuner is a nexiom.** It lit the machine on its own, so one nexiom is enough to light it.
- **Kividok, rikolu and menesol are not nexioms.** Each failed to light the machine alone.

That leaves gugaben or munavin as the second nexiom. With my last test I'll try gugaben alone. If it lights up, gugaben is the second nexiom. If it doesn't, the second nexiom is munavin.

This relies on the assumption that either nexiom can light the machine by itself. Notuner alone lighting it supports that, but it isn't fully proven.

TEST: gugaben
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

My answer is notuner and munavin. Notuner is certain, but munavin rests on an assumption I couldn't test.

- **Notuner is a nexiom.** It lit the machine on its own.
- **Munavin is the most likely second nexiom.** Kividok, rikolu, menesol and gugaben each failed to light the machine alone. Munavin is the only object I never tested alone.

This depends on assuming that either nexiom can light the machine by itself. Notuner showed that one nexiom can, but I never showed the other can too. If the machine responds to the two nexioms differently, the second nexiom could be one of the objects that failed alone. In that case I can't tell which one, and munavin is just a guess.

ANSWER: nexioms = notuner, munavin
One last question. If only munavin were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

I expect **yes**, but this rests on the same untested assumption as my answer.

If munavin is the second nexiom and the machine lights for any single nexiom, then munavin alone should light it. Notuner alone lit the machine, which shows one nexiom can be enough.

I never tested munavin alone, though, and I never confirmed that both nexioms behave the same way. If the machine treats them differently, for example lighting only for notuner, then munavin alone might not light it. Munavin might also not be a nexiom at all, if the true second nexiom is one of the objects that failed alone. In either case the answer would be no.

PROBE: yes

New machine. Its objects are: ravazol, pamaval, fitugar, gabekon, kafubik, sabasek.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects together, to see whether any nexioms are in this group.

TEST: ravazol, pamaval, fitugar
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

Nothing lit with ravazol, pamaval and fitugar together. If any single nexiom is enough to light the machine, both nexioms must be among gabekon, kafubik and sabasek. But the rule might instead need both nexioms present, so I can't rule anything out yet. Next I'll test a pair from the other half.

TEST: gabekon, kafubik
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine stayed dark for ravazol, pamaval and fitugar, but lit for gabekon and kafubik. I don't yet know whether one nexiom is enough to light it or both are needed, so both nexioms might be in gabekon/kafubik, or one might be sabasek. Testing gabekon alone will help separate these cases.

TEST: gabekon
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Results so far: ravazol, pamaval and fitugar together stayed dark. Gabekon and kafubik together lit up. Gabekon alone stayed dark.

**If one nexiom is enough to light the machine:**
- Both nexioms must be among gabekon, kafubik and sabasek, since the first test stayed dark.
- Gabekon alone stayed dark, so it is not a nexiom.
- That leaves kafubik and sabasek.
- A rule where exactly one nexiom must be present gives the same pair.

**If both nexioms are needed:**
- The lit test means they must be gabekon and kafubik.

Testing sabasek alone separates these two cases. If it lights up, the nexioms are kafubik and sabasek. If it stays dark, they are gabekon and kafubik.

TEST: sabasek
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Here is what the four results show.

- **Sabasek is a nexiom.** It lit the machine on its own, and objects that aren't nexioms never affect the machine.
- **One of gabekon or kafubik is a nexiom.** Together they lit the machine, so at least one must be a nexiom.
- **Gabekon is not a nexiom.** If it were and kafubik weren't, gabekon alone would behave the same as gabekon plus kafubik. But gabekon alone stayed dark while the pair lit up.
- **So kafubik is the other nexiom.** This fits everything else: the first test held no nexioms and stayed dark. Each single nexiom lights the machine.

ANSWER: nexioms = kafubik, sabasek
One last question. If only kafubik were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

Yes. This follows directly from the results rather than being a guess.

- **The pair test:** gabekon and kafubik together lit the machine.
- **Gabekon is not a nexiom:** objects that aren't nexioms never affect the machine. So that test behaved exactly as kafubik alone would.
- **Conclusion:** kafubik on its own lights the machine. This fits sabasek also lighting it alone. Each nexiom triggers the machine by itself, and the first test, with no nexioms, stayed dark.

PROBE: yes

New machine. Its objects are: dolugol, sukidos, bonaka, gitunun, tuladen, kisuros.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half the objects together to see how the machine responds.

TEST: dolugol, sukidos, bonaka
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The first group lit up, but I don't know the rule yet. It could light when any nexiom is present, only when both are, or when exactly one is. Testing a single object alone should help tell these apart and narrow down the candidates.

TEST: dolugol
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Dolugol lit up alone, so dolugol must be a nexiom. That also rules out the machine needing both nexioms present. It lights either when at least one nexiom is present, or when exactly one is.

Under either rule, a group without dolugol lights up only if it contains the other nexiom. That means I can search the remaining five candidates by splitting them into groups. I'll test three of them first.

TEST: sukidos, bonaka, gitunun
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The group of sukidos, bonaka and gitunun lit up without dolugol, so the second nexiom is one of those three. Testing sukidos alone will either identify it or narrow the search to bonaka and gitunun.

TEST: sukidos
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Sukidos lit up when tested alone, and non-nexioms never affect the machine, so sukidos is the second nexiom. The first test also lit up with both dolugol and sukidos on the machine. That rules out the "exactly one" rule, so the machine lights whenever at least one nexiom is present, and every result fits that rule.

ANSWER: nexioms = dolugol, sukidos
One last question. If only dolugol were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

Yes. I tested dolugol alone as my second test and the machine lit up. This was observed directly, not inferred. It also fits the rule I concluded: the machine lights whenever at least one nexiom is present.

PROBE: yes
